scan.summary: This is your own log of the daily pre-shift checks on forklift FL-2, a propane Toyota 8FGU25, for September 2026. The file is a photo, and the last row you can see is Sep 17. It shows one defect, a horn that was not working on Sep 9. There is no note saying the truck was taken out of service or repaired before the horn was marked OK the next day. There are also missing days even though the hour meter shows the truck was running. A log like this is your proof that the truck was checked before each shift and that problems were fixed before anyone used it again. It is judged on whether it is complete and up to date, not measured against a written standard.
scan.freshness_note: The last visible entry is Sep 17, 2026, which is 10 days before today (Sep 27). The photo seems to cut off at the bottom of the page, so later rows may exist but aren't shown. Ask for a complete scan of the whole September log, including any page 2 through today. You will also need the October log once the month starts.

gaps.title: Horn defect found with no record of taking the truck out of service or repairing it
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn was marked X with the note 'Horn not working'. On Sep 10 the horn is ticked OK and a different operator used the truck. Nothing in the log shows whether FL-2 was taken out of service, who repaired the horn, or when. Federal rules say a truck that is unsafe or needs repair must come out of service until it has been restored to safe condition. The log does not show that happened.
gaps.fix: Find or write the repair record: work order or maintenance entry, date, who did the repair, and confirmation the truck was tagged out in between. Staple it to the September log or reference it there. Going forward, add a 'Defect corrected / date / by' column or sign-off line so every X has a close-out entry.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (examine before each shift; report and correct defects) and 1910.178(p)(1) (a truck found in need of repair or unsafe is taken out of service until restored). Oregon OSHA enforces 1910.178 through its Division 2 rules. I think it also has Oregon-specific additions, but I have not checked the exact OAR section.
gaps.locator: page 1, Sep 9 row (Horn column and Notes) and Sep 10 row

gaps.title: No entries for Sep 3 and Sep 4, but the hour meter shows the truck was used
gaps.description: The rows go from Sep 2 (4,819 hours) straight to Sep 7 (4,834 hours). That is a 15-hour jump, while other workdays show about 6–7 hours. Sep 3 and 4 were a Thursday and Friday. This suggests FL-2 was used for about 8 hours without a logged pre-shift check (inferred from the hour meter and the calendar). The Sep 7 entry also falls on Labor Day.
gaps.fix: Ask the warehouse lead whether FL-2 ran on Sep 3–4 and whether checks were done but not written down (for example, on a missing page or a different sheet). If they weren't done, remind operators that the check happens every shift the truck is used. Consider having a supervisor review the log each week.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7). The federal rule requires the check before each shift but does not require it to be written down. The log is your evidence, so gaps in it weaken that evidence.
gaps.locator: page 1, between the Sep 2 and Sep 7 rows

gaps.title: No visible entries after Sep 17
gaps.description: The last row visible in the photo is Sep 17. The bottom of the page seems to be cut off, so Sep 18–25 entries may be there but can't be seen. As far as the file shows, the record is 10 days behind.
gaps.fix: Get a complete, uncropped scan of the whole September log. If there really are no entries after Sep 17 while the truck was in use, treat it the same as gap g2.
gaps.locator: page 1, bottom edge after the Sep 17 row

gaps.title: Operators listed by initials only, with no signature or supervisor review
gaps.description: Operators are shown only as 'M.C.' and 'J.R.'. There is no signature, full name, or supervisor sign-off, so the entries can't easily be matched to operator training and certification records.
gaps.fix: Add a key on the log that maps initials to full names, or have operators sign. Add a monthly supervisor review line. Make sure both operators have current training certifications on file.

facts.value: Toyota 8FGU25 forklift, unit FL-2, propane (LPG) powered, at the Portland warehouse
facts.affects: Brings in the forklift rules in 1910.178: operator training, daily checks, and LPG refueling and cylinder-change rules. An LPG truck running indoors also raises carbon monoxide exposure questions.

facts.value: Unit numbering 'FL-2' suggests the company has at least two forklifts
facts.affects: Each truck needs its own pre-shift log. Look for an FL-1 log.

facts.value: At least two people operate FL-2, shown by the initials M.C. and J.R. The log does not say whether they are certified.
facts.affects: Each operator needs a training and evaluation certification under 1910.178(l)(6).

facts.value: FL-2 runs day shift only, weekdays, about 6–7 hours a day
facts.affects: Sets how many pre-shift checks are expected. If other shifts use the truck, each of those shifts needs its own check.

scan.confidence_notes: Confident about: the text is clear, and the header, checklist, dates, hour readings, marks, initials and notes can all be read reliably. Probably the same document you already hold: this looks like the same September 2026 FL-2 log (a photo of it, or a fuller copy), but I can't tell which is more complete. Less sure: (1) The photo seems cropped at the bottom, so I can't say Sep 17 is really the last entry. (2) The Sep 3–4 gap comes from the hour meter and the calendar (Sep 1, 2026 is a Tuesday and Sep 7 is Labor Day). It is an inference, not something the log says. (3) Federal 1910.178 requires the pre-shift check but not a written record, so the gaps weaken your evidence rather than breaking a recordkeeping rule. The exception is the horn defect: the rule does require a defective truck to be taken out of service, and the log doesn't show that happened. (4) Oregon OSHA enforces 1910.178, and I think it may add Oregon-specific forklift rules, but I have not checked the exact OAR section.
